languages.name: Scala
languages.description: Scala 3 reference focused on functional/JVM desktop helpers, expressive modeling, collections, concurrency, and Java interoperability.

categories.name: Core Scala 3
categories.description: Expressions, values, functions, and control flow.

entries.title: val and var
entries.summary: Declare immutable values with val and mutable variables with var.
entries.signature: val name = value / var name = value
entries.definition: Declare immutable values with val and mutable variables with var.
entries.mental_model: Prefer val; reach for var only when mutation is truly useful.

entries.title: Expression-oriented blocks
entries.summary: Blocks evaluate to their final expression and can directly produce values.
entries.definition: Blocks evaluate to their final expression and can directly produce values.
entries.mental_model: Many Scala constructs produce values instead of only causing effects.

entries.title: Functions
entries.summary: Define methods with def and anonymous functions with => syntax.
entries.definition: Define methods with def and anonymous functions with => syntax.
entries.mental_model: Functions are first-class while methods belong to objects/classes.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
def double(x: Int): Int = x * 2
val triple: Int => Int = x => x * 3

entries.title: Pattern matching
entries.summary: Deconstruct values and choose branches with match/case.
entries.definition: Deconstruct values and choose branches with match/case.
entries.mental_model: Pattern matching combines branching with destructuring.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
val label = 2 match
  case 1 => "one"
  case 2 => "two"
  case _ => "other"

entries.title: for comprehensions
entries.summary: Compose map/flatMap/filter-style operations with readable syntax.
entries.definition: Compose map/flatMap/filter-style operations with readable syntax.
entries.mental_model: Syntactic sugar for functional collection/monadic composition.

examples.title: Example
examples.code: val doubled = for n <- List(1,2,3) yield n * 2

categories.name: Modeling and Type System
categories.description: Algebraic data types and reusable abstractions.

entries.title: Case classes
entries.summary: Define concise immutable data models with structural equality and pattern matching support.
entries.definition: Define concise immutable data models with structural equality and pattern matching support.
entries.mental_model: Product types with generated ergonomic machinery.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
case class Macro(key: String, language: String)
val m = Macro("M5", "Scala")

entries.title: Enums
entries.summary: Define closed families of values and algebraic data types.
entries.definition: Define closed families of values and algebraic data types.
entries.mental_model: A finite set of alternatives that pattern matching can exhaust.

entries.title: Traits
entries.summary: Define reusable interfaces and behavior that classes/objects can extend.
entries.definition: Define reusable interfaces and behavior that classes/objects can extend.
entries.mental_model: Traits are composable capabilities with optional implementation.

entries.title: Option
entries.summary: Represent a value that may be present or absent without null.
entries.definition: Represent a value that may be present or absent without null.
entries.mental_model: Absence is an explicit branch in the type.

entries.title: Either
entries.summary: Represent a computation that yields one of two typed outcomes, commonly error or success.
entries.definition: Represent a computation that yields one of two typed outcomes, commonly error or success.

entries.title: given / using
entries.summary: Provide and consume contextual values in Scala 3.
entries.definition: Provide and consume contextual values in Scala 3.
entries.mental_model: The compiler can thread ambient capabilities explicitly through types.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
given Ordering[String] = Ordering.String
val xs = List("b","a").sorted

entries.title: Extension methods
entries.summary: Add callable syntax to existing types without modifying them.
entries.definition: Add callable syntax to existing types without modifying them.
entries.mental_model: Static helper behavior with instance-like call syntax.

examples.title: Example
examples.code:
extension (s: String)
  def shout: String = s.toUpperCase + "!"
println("wyn".shout)
